lag_vongole_produktion.name: Farmed Manila clams in the Venice Lagoon
lag_vongole_produktion.note: Harvest in the sub-concessions granted by San Servolo srl (successor to GRAL), 2019; in addition an estimated 661 tonnes from fishing on free banks. In 2015 production was 3,613 tonnes (Osservatorio, 2016 report). The species Ruditapes philippinarum was released in the southern lagoon in 1983 (200,000 juveniles).

lag_vongole_topp_1999.name: Clam harvest in the lagoon at its peak, 1998–1999
lag_vongole_topp_1999.note: From an estimated 1,300 tonnes in 1990 to about 40,000 tonnes in 1998–1999 (Boatto & Pellizzato 2005); in 2007 the lagoon produced half of Italy's output, and including illegal fishing the harvest was estimated at about 30,000 tonnes a year. Mechanical fishing ploughed up the bottom and is named as the main cause of erosion in 1970–2002 (Sarretta et al. 2010).

lag_vongole_koncessioner_ha.name: Lagoon area leased for clam farming
lag_vongole_koncessioner_ha.note: 104 sub-concessions in the northern, central and southern lagoon, about 2.5% of the lagoon area (own calculation: 14.04 / 550 km²), employing 547 members. In 2015 there were 67 cooperatives with 457 workers, 50 vibrating harvest boats and 255 small boats (Osservatorio 2016).

lag_vongole_varde.name: First-sale value of farmed clams in the lagoon
lag_vongole_varde.note: 2,159 tonnes × €6.50/kg (average producer price at the Venice fish market in 2019) ≈ €14.0 million. Veneto Agricoltura puts the average income at €25,655 per farmer in 2019.

lag_valli_da_pesca.name: Fish farms (valli da pesca) in the Venice Lagoon
lag_valli_da_pesca.note: 28 embanked fish farms: 18 in the northern lagoon (5,781 ha, 3,906 ha of it water) and 10 in the southern (3,503 ha, 2,860 ha water), according to Federvalli Veneto 2014 (own sum). The whole of Veneto has 58 valli on 20,149 ha, with yields of 100–150 kg of fish per ha (eel, sea bass, gilthead bream, mullet). The World Heritage plan gives 83 km² of fish farms.

lag_fiskeforetag_provins.name: Businesses in sea and lagoon fishing, province of Venice
lag_fiskeforetag_provins.note: 594 businesses with 1,271 people employed in sea and lagoon fishing in 2019 (Infocamere); the whole fishing primary sector has 829 businesses and 1,572 employed. In the lagoon there were 98 permits for fixed gear (9 cooperatives, 87.8 km of nets), 15 licences for fry fishing and 20 mussel farms. The number of boats was not found.

lag_grossistmarknad_fisk.name: Fish sold at the Venice wholesale market (Tronchetto)
lag_grossistmarknad_fisk.note: Just under 7,000 tonnes in 2022 (−8% on 2021) worth just over €58 million; volume has fallen by about 2.5% a year since 2000. 24 selling firms and about 215 buyers (60% fishmongers, 25% street vendors, 10% restaurants), with fish from the Adriatic and far away. The municipality plans a new market building on Isola Nova del Tronchetto.

lag_rialto_fiskstand.name: Fish stalls at the Rialto market (Pescheria)
lag_rialto_fiskstand.note: According to a motion in the city council (January 2024): about thirty fish stalls in the 1980s, seven today; fruit and vegetable stalls have gone from 90 to fewer than 13 (IUAV study) and butchers from 27 to 2. The motion describes the Pescheria building of 1907 (Domenico Rupolo) as empty since 2008. A political document; the figures are not official statistics.

lag_santerasmo_kronartskocka.name: Growers in the Slow Food Presidium Carciofo violetto di Sant'Erasmo
lag_santerasmo_kronartskocka.note: Fourteen named producers of the violet artichoke on Sant'Erasmo and on land on Vignole, Mazzorbo and Lio Piccolo. The island is 'half the size of the city' and has been 'one vast vegetable garden' since the 16th century; the season starts in late April with the castraure, the plant's first top shoot. Area and harvest are not given.

lag_venissa_vingard.name: The Venissa vineyard on Mazzorbo
lag_venissa_vingard.note: A walled vineyard (vigna murata) of under 1 ha with the local Dorona grape: about 4,000 vines, about 4,000 bottles a year and a first vintage in 2010 (Drinks International 2014). It was started by Gianluca Bisol; vines came from Sant'Erasmo among other places (Wine Economist 2014). Trade press, no official figures.

lag_gronyta_per_invanare.name: Urban green space per inhabitant, municipality of Venice
lag_gronyta_per_invanare.note: Publicly managed green space, 12.15 km², divided by the average population (table 12.1); 42.8 m² in 2011. The average for Italy's provincial capitals is 33.7 m² and for north-east Italy 64.3 m² (2024). 41% of the green space is protected historic green and 20% urban forestry; the figure covers the whole municipality including Mestre.

lag_tillganglig_gronyta.name: Accessible green space (verde fruibile) per inhabitant
lag_tillganglig_gronyta.note: Parks, historic green, equipped areas, school gardens, outdoor sports areas and cemeteries, 8.45 km² (tables 14.1–14.2). The average for provincial capitals is 15.9 m². ISTAT's report for 2023 singled out Venice as best among the large cities (then 35.5 m²).

lag_gronyta_andel.name: Urban green space as a share of the municipal area
lag_gronyta_andel.note: 12.15 km² of the municipal area, much of which is lagoon water (table 11.1); the average for provincial capitals is 3.0%. There are no separate figures for the historic centre. In OpenStreetMap the model square (1.8 × 1.8 km) has 3.8 ha of parks and 1.4 ha of gardens, including the Giardini Reali at 0.46 ha (own calculation; private gardens and cloisters are incompletely mapped).

lag_trad_per_100_invanare.name: Inventoried trees per 100 inhabitants
lag_trad_per_100_invanare.note: 70,546 trees in the municipality's inventory of public green space (parts of the municipality, updated 2024; table 2.1). The average for provincial capitals is 24.4 and for north-east Italy 62.1. 506 trees were felled in 2024 and 428 in 2023 (table 5.1); the model square has 470 trees in OpenStreetMap (own count, incomplete).

lag_hardgjord_mark_andel.name: Sealed and built-up land (suolo consumato)
lag_hardgjord_mark_andel.note: 7,164 ha of artificial surface out of the municipality's total area, much of which is lagoon. Veneto 11.86%, Italy 7.17% and the province of Venice 14.10% (2024). The historic centre is not reported separately.

lag_hardgjord_okning.name: Net increase of sealed land 2023–2024
lag_hardgjord_okning.note: Gross 65.18 ha of new development, 0.97 ha restored. The sum of ISPRA's net increases 2006–2024 is about 486 ha (own sum of eleven periods).

lag_avfall_per_invanare.name: Municipal waste per inhabitant
lag_avfall_per_invanare.note: 173,318 tonnes divided by 249,466 inhabitants; visitors' waste is counted against residents, hence the high value. Veneto 524.95 kg and Italy 507.90 kg (2024); 709 kg in 2010.

lag_sorteringsgrad.name: Share of separately collected waste (raccolta differenziata)
lag_sorteringsgrad.note: 110,442 of 173,318 tonnes; 32.65% in 2010 and a high of 65.98% in 2020. Veneto 78.16%, Italy 67.69% (2024); the legal target is 65%. Venice is third among cities over 200,000 inhabitants after Bologna and Padua.

lag_dorrhamtning_andel.name: Households with door-to-door waste collection (porta a porta)
lag_dorrhamtning_andel.note: 29% of household customers have door-to-door collection, 71% use street bins. In the historic centre dry recyclables have also been collected at the door since 2016: collectors walk with light carts to compactor boats, and residents bring 35–50% of the weight themselves to 60 fixed points at set times (municipality 2023). In high season about 330 litter bins are emptied almost hourly using five motor boats.

lag_avlopp_anpassningar.name: Approved sewage adaptations in the historic centre (septic tanks, small treatment plants)
lag_avlopp_anpassningar.note: Almost 1,800 adaptations approved by the Magistrato alle Acque, mostly septic tanks and grease traps for hotels, bars and restaurants under the special laws 71/90, 360/91 and 206/95, plus 85 small treatment plants for discharges above 100 p.e.; more than 1,100 projects were under way, about 2,900 plans in total. Otherwise the sewage reaches the canals through septic tanks and the old tunnels (gatoli); no share of households connected to a central treatment plant was found.

lag_septiktank_krav.name: Required septic tank volume per person in the historic city
lag_septiktank_krav.note: Since the 1933 hygiene regulation, buildings discharging to a canal or to the gatoli must have a septic tank before the outlet; the volume of 0.4 m³ per person served was set in DPR 962/1973 and was still applied in 2004. The municipality requires adaptation when an owner applies for a permit to renovate; the gatoli were on average half blocked.

lag_marghera_sin.name: Contaminated site of national interest (SIN) Venezia–Porto Marghera
lag_marghera_sin.note: Now covers land areas only. Before the 2013 redefinition (DM 144/2013, corrected 2016) it included 3,221 ha of land, 350 ha of port channels and 2,200 ha of lagoon. Refining, petrochemicals and steelworks have left metals and PAHs in the soil and metals, PAHs and chlorinated organics in the groundwater; agreements on containment works were signed in 2020.

lag_mikroplast_sediment.name: Microplastics in lagoon sediments (highest measured level)
lag_mikroplast_sediment.note: 672–2,175 particles smaller than 1 mm per kg of sediment at ten sampling sites, highest near the mainland; polyethylene and polypropylene make up more than 82% and 93% are 30–500 µm in size. A single survey, no time series.

lag_unesco_inskrivet.name: Venice and its Lagoon inscribed on UNESCO's World Heritage List
lag_unesco_inskrivet.note: World Heritage property no. 394, inscribed in 1987 under all six cultural criteria (i)–(vi) (UNESCO state-of-conservation document 2021); the area coincides with the landscape protection under the Ministerial Decree of 1 August 1985 and covers the lagoon municipalities. There is no buffer zone: the Committee referred the proposal back in 2019 and did not approve the new one in 2026 (decision 48 COM 8B.45).

lag_unesco_bevarandebeslut.name: World Heritage Committee state-of-conservation decisions on Venice 2014–2026
lag_unesco_bevarandebeslut.note: 38 COM 7B.27 (2014), 40 COM 7B.52 (2016), 41 COM 7B.48 (2017), 43 COM 7B.86 (2019), 44 COM 7B.50 (2021), 45 COM 7B.189 (2023), 47 COM 7B.113 (2025) and 48 COM 7B.40 (2026) – own count. The drafts of 2021 and 2023 proposed the List of World Heritage in Danger but the Committee adopted amended decisions; in 2025 and 2026 it warned that the conditions for such a listing may be met unless binding rules on tourism, building heights and impact assessment are introduced. The next report is due on 1 February 2027.

lag_kulturminnesmarkta_byggnader.name: Listed buildings (edifici notificati)
lag_kulturminnesmarkta_byggnader.note: According to the then Soprintendente Renata Codello, the Venice Soprintendenza is Italy's smallest by area but the densest in protected buildings; the whole area has also been under landscape protection since 1985, so every intervention needs the authority's permission. A current number of churches and palaces in a primary source was not found.

lag_byggnader_fore_1919.name: Residential buildings built before 1919 in the historic centre
lag_byggnader_fore_1919.note: 6,960 of 8,375 residential buildings in the districts San Marco–Castello–S. Elena–Cannaregio and Dorsoduro–S. Polo–S. Croce–Giudecca–Sacca Fisola (57,449 inhabitants in 2011); 89.6% date from before 1946 and 98% have load-bearing masonry. Whole municipality 26.6%, Veneto 11.7%, Italy 15.0% (same census, own sum).

lag_byggnader_daligt_skick.name: Residential buildings in mediocre or poor condition in the historic centre
lag_byggnader_daligt_skick.note: 2,151 buildings in 'mediocre' and 88 in 'poor' condition out of 8,375 (own sum from the 2011 census). Italy 16.8%, Veneto 12.6% and the whole municipality 13.1%.

lag_solceller_byggar_grans.name: Solar panels banned on buildings built before 1945 in the historic city
lag_solceller_byggar_grans.note: The municipality's rule summary (March 2022, building regulation art. 38.6): solar PV and thermal panels are forbidden on buildings from before 1945 in the Città Antica. On later buildings they are allowed only on flat surfaces such as roofs, terraces and roof slabs (lastrici solari) – never on pitches clad with coppi tiles – and new buildings may only have panels integrated in the roof pitch; on the islands and the mainland the rules are more permissive.

lag_hojning_max_cm.name: Largest practical raising of streets and quays in historic districts
lag_hojning_max_cm.note: At Rialto the protection level of +100 cm above the Punta della Salute datum was chosen, since the ground in places lies at only +70 cm. Raising by more than 15–20 cm is almost never possible: the number of critical thresholds rises from 6 at +100 cm to 21 at +110 and 51 at +120 cm, and the same applies to ground-floor floors.

lag_forsamlingar_centro_storico.name: Catholic parishes in the historic centre
lag_forsamlingar_centro_storico.note: In 2025 the Patriarchate merged 19 parishes into 6, each with several churches, because of population decline (under 50,000 inhabitants), fewer priests and lower participation. 17 churches charge admission through the Chorus association (the Patriarch in Finestre sull'Arte 2023). A reliable number of churches in the historic centre was not found.

nt_folkmangd.name: Population of the Comune di Venezia
nt_folkmangd.note: Registered residents on 1 January 2026 (ISTAT, provisional); 249,490 on 1 January 2025 and 256,083 on 1 January 2021. The municipality's own register counts slightly more (251,295 in 2025) because ISTAT adjusts its figures to the census. Italy 58,942,828, Veneto 4,857,460 (2026).

nt_befolkningsforandring_1ar.name: Population change, past year
nt_befolkningsforandring_1ar.note: Own calculation: (249,385 − 249,490) / 249,490 = −0.04% between 1 January 2025 and 1 January 2026 (ISTAT, provisional). The natural decrease (1,409 births, 3,345 deaths) was almost offset by in-migration, mainly from abroad (+2,414 net). Italy −0.001%, Veneto +0.08% (2025, own calculation).

nt_befolkningsforandring_5ar.name: Population change, past five years
nt_befolkningsforandring_5ar.note: Own calculation: (249,385 − 256,083) / 256,083 = −2.62% between 1 January 2021 and 1 January 2026 (ISTAT; 2026 provisional). Italy −0.50%, Veneto −0.25% (2021–2026, own calculation; Veneto's 2021 population from Eurostat demo_r_gind3).

nt_folkmangd_centro_storico.name: Population of Venice's historic centre (centro storico)
nt_folkmangd_centro_storico.note: Registered residents of the centro storico (San Marco, Castello, Sant'Elena, Cannaregio, Dorsoduro, San Polo, Santa Croce and Giudecca) in the municipal register, 2025; the table gives the year but not the date. 55,589 in 2015 (−14.3%); over the decade 2,797 were born and 8,810 died. Italy and Veneto: not applicable; the whole municipality had 251,295 residents in the same register (2025).

nt_medelalder_centro_storico.name: Mean age in the centro storico
nt_medelalder_centro_storico.note: The mean age of registered residents of the centro storico rose from 49.3 years in 2015 to 51.4 in 2025; the whole municipality 48.7 and the mainland (terraferma) 47.5 years. The mean age of Italy and Veneto is not in the same source; for comparison, the median age: Italy 49.1, Veneto 49.6 years (2025, Eurostat).

nt_medianalder.name: Median age
nt_medianalder.note: Median age on 1 January 2025 in Eurostat's city statistics (Urban Audit, built on ISTAT data), unchanged since 2022. Italy 49.1, Veneto 49.6 years (2025, Eurostat demo_r_pjanind2).

nt_andel_0_19.name: Share of inhabitants aged 0–19
nt_andel_0_19.note: Own calculation from ISTAT's single-year ages: 37,448 of 249,490 inhabitants were aged 0–19 on 1 January 2025 (14.9% in the provisional 2026 figures). Italy 16.9%, Veneto 16.7% (2025, Eurostat).

nt_andel_65_plus.name: Share of inhabitants aged 65+
nt_andel_65_plus.note: Own calculation from ISTAT's single-year ages: 71,091 of 249,490 inhabitants were 65 or older on 1 January 2025 (28.7% in the provisional 2026 figures). Italy 24.7%, Veneto 24.9% (2025, Eurostat).

nt_andel_80_plus.name: Share of inhabitants aged 80+
nt_andel_80_plus.note: Own calculation from ISTAT's single-year ages: 25,810 of 249,490 inhabitants were 80 or older on 1 January 2025 (also 10.3% in the provisional 2026 figures). Italy 7.8%, Veneto 8.0% (2025, Eurostat).

nt_forsorjningskvot.name: Demographic dependency ratio ((0–19 + 65+) / 20–64)
nt_forsorjningskvot.note: Own calculation: (37,448 + 71,091) / 140,951 = 0.77 on 1 January 2025, i.e. 0.77 children, young people and older people per person of working age. Italy 0.71, Veneto 0.71 (2025, Eurostat demo_r_pjanind2, variant 3).

nt_fodda_per_1000.name: Live births per 1,000 inhabitants
nt_fodda_per_1000.note: Live births per 1,000 inhabitants: 1,421 births in 2024 (Eurostat city statistics, break in series 2024). ISTAT's provisional 2025 balance gives 1,409 births. Italy 6.3, Veneto 6.2 (2024, Eurostat demo_r_gind3).

nt_doda_per_1000.name: Deaths per 1,000 inhabitants
nt_doda_per_1000.note: Deaths per 1,000 inhabitants: 3,354 deaths in 2024 and 3,345 in 2025 in ISTAT's provisional balance; the rate reflects the old population. Italy 11.1, Veneto 10.4 (2024, Eurostat demo_r_gind3).

nt_flyttnetto_per_1000.name: Net migration per 1,000 inhabitants
nt_flyttnetto_per_1000.note: Own calculation from ISTAT's 2024 demographic balance: total change −800 minus the natural decrease −1,933 gives +1,133 (net migration including statistical adjustment), divided by the mean population of 249,890 = 4.5 per 1,000. Abroad gave +1,404 and the rest of Italy −283. Italy 4.3, Veneto 4.5 (2024, Eurostat demo_r_gind3).

nt_hushall_antal.name: Number of households
nt_hushall_antal.note: Households (famiglie anagrafiche) on 31 December 2024 according to ISTAT; 247,232 people lived in households, on average 1.96 per household (own calculation), and 2,258 in institutions. Italy and Veneto: no comparison fetched (a count, 2024).

nt_befolkningstathet.name: Population density
nt_befolkningstathet.note: Own calculation: 249,490 inhabitants (1 January 2025, ISTAT) / 418.4 km² (the whole municipal area according to ISPRA) = 596 inhabitants/km². The area includes much of the lagoon, so density on the mainland and the islands is far higher. Italy 198.0, Veneto 279.7 inhabitants/km² (2024, Eurostat demo_r_d3dens).

nt_medellivslangd_man.name: Life expectancy, men
nt_medellivslangd_man.note: Life expectancy at birth for men in the province (the Metropolitan City of Venice), provisional; not published for the municipality. 78.1 years in 2004 and 80.3 in the pandemic year 2020. Italy 81.4, Veneto 82.2 years (2024).

nt_medellivslangd_kvinnor.name: Life expectancy, women
nt_medellivslangd_kvinnor.note: Life expectancy at birth for women in the province, provisional; 84.1 years in 2004. Both sexes together 84.0 years. Italy 85.5, Veneto 86.3 years (2024).

nt_undvikbar_dodlighet.name: Avoidable mortality, ages 0–74
nt_undvikbar_dodlighet.note: Deaths before age 75 from causes that can be prevented or treated (the OECD/Eurostat list), age-standardised per 10,000 inhabitants of the province. Italy 17.6, Veneto 15.2 (2022).

nt_sjukhussangar_per_10000.name: Hospital beds per 10,000 inhabitants
nt_sjukhussangar_per_10000.note: Hospital beds (ordinary, day hospital and day surgery) in public and accredited private hospitals per 10,000 inhabitants of the province (ISTAT from Ministry of Health data). Italy 33.3, Veneto 32.3 (2022).

nt_specialistlakare_per_10000.name: Specialist doctors per 10,000 inhabitants
nt_specialistlakare_per_10000.note: Specialist doctors working in public and private care per 10,000 inhabitants of the province; GPs and primary-care paediatricians are not included (ISTAT from IQVIA OneKey). Italy 34.1, Veneto 29.6 (2023).

nt_hogskoleutbildade_25_64.name: Tertiary education, ages 25–64
nt_hogskoleutbildade_25_64.note: Own calculation from Eurostat city statistics: 35,458 of 129,073 residents aged 25–64 (the sum of the three education levels) had tertiary education (ISCED 5–8) in 2023. The city figure rests on ISTAT's register-based census, the comparisons on the labour force survey. Italy 21.6%, Veneto 20.5% (2023, Eurostat edat_lfse_04).

nt_hogskoleutbildade_25_39.name: Tertiary degree, ages 25–39
nt_hogskoleutbildade_25_39.note: Share of 25–39-year-olds in the province with a tertiary degree (ISCED 5–8), ISTAT labour force survey. Italy 30.9%, Veneto 34.4% (2024).

nt_tidiga_skolavhopp.name: Early leavers from education and training (18–24)
nt_tidiga_skolavhopp.note: Share of 18–24-year-olds with at most lower secondary education who are not in education or training (labour force survey); published for regions only. The EU target for 2030 is below 9%. Italy 8.2%, Veneto 7.6% (2025).

nt_neet_15_29.name: Young people aged 15–29 neither in work nor in education (NEET)
nt_neet_15_29.note: Share of 15–29-year-olds in the province neither in work nor in education or training (ISTAT, labour force survey). For the regions 2025 is available: Italy 13.3%, Veneto 8.3% (Eurostat edat_lfse_22). Italy 15.2%, Veneto 9.0% (2024).

nt_forskoleplatser_0_2.name: Places in nurseries and other early childcare per 100 children aged 0–2
nt_forskoleplatser_0_2.note: Authorised places in nurseries (asili nido) and supplementary early-childhood services per 100 children aged 0–2, school year 2024/25 (ISTAT database, year 2024): 12.0 public and 28.5 private, 1,847 places in 58 services. ISTAT compares with the EU target of 45% participation by 2030. Italy 33.2, Veneto: not fetched (2024/25).

nt_sysselsattningsgrad_15_64.name: Employment rate, ages 15–64 (province)
nt_sysselsattningsgrad_15_64.note: Employed share of 15–64-year-olds in the province according to the labour force survey (68.1% in 2024); for the municipality the census gives 69.1% (nt_sysselsattningsgrad_kommun). Italy 62.5%, Veneto 69.3% (2025).

nt_arbetsloshet_15_74.name: Unemployment rate, ages 15–74 (province)
nt_arbetsloshet_15_74.note: Unemployed as a percentage of the labour force aged 15–74 in the province, labour force survey (3.9% in 2024). Italy 6.1%, Veneto 3.4% (2025).

nt_sysselsattningsgrad_kommun.name: Employment rate, ages 15–64 (municipality, census)
nt_sysselsattningsgrad_kommun.note: Own calculation from the permanent census on 31 December 2024: 105,084 employed of 152,138 residents aged 15–64. The census rests on registers and a sample and differs from the labour force survey. Italy 63.4%, Veneto 70.0% (2024, same source and calculation).

nt_arbetsloshet_kommun.name: Unemployment rate, ages 15+ (municipality, census)
nt_arbetsloshet_kommun.note: Own calculation from the permanent census on 31 December 2024: 6,124 job seekers out of a labour force of 116,838 aged 15 and over; 2023 gives 5.4% (Eurostat city statistics: 5.39%). Italy 7.2%, Veneto 4.7% (2024, same source and calculation).

nt_beskattningsbar_inkomst.name: Taxable income per taxpayer (mean)
nt_beskattningsbar_inkomst.note: Own calculation from the income tax returns for 2024: taxable income of €5,156,700,571 for 190,227 taxpayers with taxable income (200,207 taxpayers in all). A mean, not a median. Italy €24,893, Veneto €25,885 (2024, summed over all municipalities in the same file).

nt_disponibel_inkomst_per_inv.name: Household disposable income per inhabitant (province)
nt_disponibel_inkomst_per_inv.note: Household disposable income per inhabitant of the province, current prices (Istituto Tagliacarne's provincial estimates in ISTAT's BES dei territori). Italy €22,359, Veneto €24,103 (2023).

nt_bnp_per_invanare.name: GDP per inhabitant (province)
nt_bnp_per_invanare.note: GDP per inhabitant of the province (NUTS 3 ITH35), current prices; 40,200 in purchasing power standards (PPS). Italy and Veneto also have 2024: €37,300 and €41,500. Italy €36,300, Veneto €40,700 (2023).

nt_fattigdom_social_utestangning.name: At risk of poverty or social exclusion (Veneto)
nt_fattigdom_social_utestangning.note: Share of the population with low income, severe material and social deprivation or very low work intensity (EU-SILC, AROPE); published for regions only. Veneto had 12.4% the year before. Italy 22.6%, Veneto 14.6% (2025).

nt_gastnatter_per_invanare.name: Overnight stays per inhabitant
nt_gastnatter_per_invanare.note: Nights spent in tourist accommodation (hotels and other, ISTAT tourism statistics via Eurostat) per inhabitant: 12,925,741 nights in 2025, 11,195,100 of them by foreign guests; break in series 2024. Day visitors are not included. Italy 9.1, Veneto 15.3 (2025, own calculation from Eurostat tour_occ_nin2 and the population on 1 January 2025).

nt_baddar_per_1000.name: Bed places in tourist accommodation per 1,000 inhabitants
nt_baddar_per_1000.note: Bed places in tourist accommodation per 1,000 inhabitants: 91,556 bed places in 2025 against 77,037 in 2022 (break in series 2024). Italy 130, Veneto 169 (2025, own calculation from Eurostat tour_cap_nuts2; Italy's bed places rose from 5.5 to 7.7 million in 2024–2025, which suggests a break in series).

nt_tomma_bostader.name: Dwellings without registered residents
nt_tomma_bostader.note: Own calculation from the 2021 census: 25,627 of 148,319 dwellings had no registered residents (second homes, tourist lets, empty). The permanent census for 2023 gives 26,538 of 149,294 (17.8%). Italy 27.2%, Veneto 22.0% (2021, own calculation from Eurostat cens_21dwob_r3).

nt_bostadspris.name: Average housing price (OMI)
nt_bostadspris.note: OMI's average quoted value for homes in the municipality (mean of the central values of all OMI zones), +0.5% on 2024; 3,968 homes were sold in 2025. The rest of the province €1,454/m². Italy: no corresponding national value in OMI's reports; Veneto €1,975/m² in its provincial capitals (2025).

nt_bostadspris_centro_storico.name: Average housing price in the centro storico (OMI)
nt_bostadspris_centro_storico.note: OMI's average quoted value in the Centro storico e Giudecca macro-area in 2025 (+0.4%), highest in the San Marco zone (€5,388/m²); Lido 3,308, the minor islands 2,481 and the mainland €1,660/m². Italy: no national value; Veneto €1,975/m² in its provincial capitals (2025, a different basis).

nt_vaxthusgaser_per_inv.name: Territorial greenhouse gas emissions per inhabitant (CO2, methane, nitrous oxide)
nt_vaxthusgaser_per_inv.note: Own calculation from INEMAR Veneto 2023: 4,031.8 kt CO2, 2,441 t methane and 296 t nitrous oxide = 4,179 kt CO2e (GWP100, IPCC AR5) divided by the mean population of 250,602. Two thirds come from power and energy production at Fusina and Porto Marghera. Italy 6.4 (2023, Eurostat, excluding land use), Veneto 5.8 t (2023, own calculation from INEMAR).

nt_vaxthusgaser_energi_per_inv.name: Emissions from power and energy production per inhabitant
nt_vaxthusgaser_energi_per_inv.note: Own calculation from INEMAR Veneto 2023, macro-sector 1 (energy production and fuel transformation): 2,819.8 kt CO2e / 250,602 inhabitants. Of this, 1,649 kt CO2 came from coal and 951 kt from natural gas; the power is used far beyond the municipality. Italy 1.3 (2023, fuel combustion in energy industries, Eurostat env_air_gge), Veneto 0.67 t (2023, own calculation from INEMAR).

nt_vaxthusgaser_vagtrafik_per_inv.name: Emissions from road transport per inhabitant
nt_vaxthusgaser_vagtrafik_per_inv.note: Own calculation from INEMAR Veneto 2023, macro-sector 7 (road transport): 279.5 kt CO2e / 250,602 inhabitants. Ships, aircraft and mobile machinery (macro-sector 8) emitted another 288.6 kt. Italy 1.7 (2023, road transport, Eurostat env_air_gge), Veneto 1.9 t (2023, own calculation from INEMAR).

nt_vaxthusgaser_industri_per_inv.name: Emissions from industry per inhabitant
nt_vaxthusgaser_industri_per_inv.note: Own calculation from INEMAR Veneto 2023, macro-sectors 3 and 4 (combustion in industry and process emissions): 236.5 kt CO2e / 250,602 inhabitants. Italy 1.2 (2023, manufacturing combustion and industrial processes, Eurostat env_air_gge), Veneto 1.3 t (2023, own calculation from INEMAR).

nt_fornybar_el_andel.name: Renewable share of electricity consumption (province)
nt_fornybar_el_andel.note: Renewable electricity production as a percentage of the province's gross electricity consumption (Terna via ISTAT's BES dei territori); the province has large fossil-fuelled power plants (see nt_vaxthusgaser_energi_per_inv). Italy 36.9%, Veneto 26.8% (2023).

nt_solceller_kw_per_1000.name: Installed solar PV capacity per 1,000 inhabitants
nt_solceller_kw_per_1000.note: Capacity of all solar PV installations in the municipality per 1,000 inhabitants (140.5 in 2022), about 59 MW in all (own calculation); net production was 174.5 kWh per inhabitant in 2024. Italy 272.3 kW in its provincial capitals (north-east Italy's 402.8); Veneto 239.7–576.5 kW in its other six provincial capitals (2024).

nt_elanvandning_per_inv.name: Electricity drawn from the distribution grid per inhabitant
nt_elanvandning_per_inv.note: ISTAT reports 51.3 tonnes of oil equivalent per 100 inhabitants (1,490.8 GWh), the highest of the 14 metropolitan capitals; at 11.63 MWh per tonne that is 5.97 MWh per inhabitant (own conversion). Households and businesses are included; the household share is only shown in an ISTAT chart. Italy 3.94 MWh in its provincial capitals; Veneto 2.73–10.04 MWh in its other provincial capitals (2024, own conversion).

nt_avfall_per_inv.name: Municipal waste per inhabitant
nt_avfall_per_inv.note: Municipal waste (rifiuti urbani) collected per inhabitant: 173,318 tonnes in 2024, against 651.7 kg per inhabitant in 2023. Tourists add to the waste but not to the denominator. Italy 507.9, Veneto 525.0 kg (2024).

nt_utsortering_andel.name: Separately collected waste (raccolta differenziata)
nt_utsortering_andel.note: Share of municipal waste collected separately for recycling, 110,442 tonnes in 2024 (63.0% in 2023). The legal target of 65% applied from 2012. Italy 67.7%, Veneto 78.2% (2024).

nt_vatten_per_inv.name: Drinking water supplied per inhabitant per day
nt_vatten_per_inv.note: Water supplied for authorised uses in the municipal network per inhabitant per day (ISTAT water census 2022); tourists and commuters are in the consumption but not in the denominator. 517 litres per inhabitant per day were fed into the network. Italy 236 litres in its provincial capitals (north-east Italy's 215); Veneto 207–255 litres in its other provincial capitals (2022).

nt_vattenforluster.name: Water losses in the distribution network
nt_vattenforluster.unit: % of water fed into the network
nt_vattenforluster.note: Difference between water fed into and supplied from the municipal network, as a percentage of the water fed in (42.0% in both 2018 and 2020); the province 37.9%. Italy 42.4%, Veneto 42.2% (2022, all municipalities, ISTAT's BES dei territori).

nt_bilar_per_1000.name: Passenger cars per 1,000 inhabitants
nt_bilar_per_1000.note: Registered passenger cars per 1,000 inhabitants (ISTAT from the ACI register; Eurostat city statistics give 443.85 for the same year). The centro storico has no streets for cars. The provincial capitals average 651. Italy 701, Veneto 680 (2024, Eurostat tran_r_vehst).

nt_elbilar_andel.name: Share of electric cars in the passenger car fleet
nt_elbilar_andel.note: Fully electric cars: 8.2 per 1,000 passenger cars (6.9 in 2023); hybrid cars 97.7 per 1,000. The provincial capitals average 8.1 per 1,000. Italy 0.68%, Veneto 0.71% (2024, Eurostat tran_r_elvehst).

nt_kollektivtrafik_platskm.name: Public transport supply (seat-km per inhabitant)
nt_kollektivtrafik_platskm.note: Seat-kilometres by bus, tram and boat per inhabitant: 2,486.5 million seat-km in 2024 (10,522 per inhabitant in 2023), 4,354 per inhabitant of them on the water. Italy 4,699 in its provincial capitals (2024); Veneto 5,144 in its provincial capitals (2023, BES).

nt_kollektivtrafik_resor.name: Public transport trips per inhabitant
nt_kollektivtrafik_resor.note: Public transport boardings per inhabitant: 176.8 million trips in 2024; tourists and commuters make many of them but only residents are in the denominator. Italy 176.4 in its provincial capitals (north-east Italy's 193.6); Veneto 12.0–178.9 in its other provincial capitals (2024).

nt_vattenburen_kollektivtrafik.name: Waterborne public transport (seat-km per inhabitant)
nt_vattenburen_kollektivtrafik.note: Supply of the vaporetto and ferry services: 1,088 million seat-km in 2024, 44% of the city's public transport and 98% of all waterborne public transport in Italy's provincial capitals (own calculation: 1,088 / 1,106). Italy 63 in its provincial capitals (north-east Italy's 341); Veneto: no other provincial capital has such services (2024).

nt_cykelvag_per_inv.name: Cycle paths per inhabitant
nt_cykelvag_per_inv.note: Own calculation: 190 km of cycle paths (ISTAT) / 249,490 inhabitants = 0.76 m; they are on the mainland and the Lido, cycling is not allowed in the centro storico. Density is 45.4 km per 100 km² of municipal area. Italy 31.3 km per 100 km² in its provincial capitals; Veneto 18.3–219.3 in its other provincial capitals (2024).

nt_gronyta_per_inv.name: Public urban green space per inhabitant
nt_gronyta_per_inv.note: Managed urban green space (parks, gardens, sports grounds, urban woodland and more) per inhabitant; 33.8 m² is open to the public. The lagoon's natural areas are not counted. Italy 33.7 m² in its provincial capitals (2024); Veneto 36.8 m² in its provincial capitals (2023, BES).

nt_skyddad_natur_andel.name: Protected nature, share of the municipal area
nt_skyddad_natur_andel.note: Protected natural areas (Natura 2000 and the national list) as a percentage of the municipal area, mainly the lagoon; with the city's green spaces 65.3%. The province 23.7% (2022, land only). Italy 16.8% in its provincial capitals (2024); for the whole country and Veneto 21.7% and 22.7% (2022, BES, land only).

nt_markanvandning_exploaterad_andel.name: Land take (consumo di suolo), share of the area
nt_markanvandning_exploaterad_andel.note: Land covered by buildings, roads and other artificial surfaces: 7,164 ha, 17.2% of the whole municipal area including the lagoon; the province 14.1%. Italy 7.17%, Veneto 11.86% (2024).

nt_markanvandning_okning.name: New land take in the past year
nt_markanvandning_okning.note: Net increase 2023–2024 (65.2 ha newly taken, 1.0 ha restored), the largest single-year increase since annual measurement began in 2015; 486 ha net in 2006–2024 (own sum). Italy 7,850 ha, Veneto 655 ha (2023–2024).

nt_oversvamningsrisk_befolkning.name: Residents in areas of medium flood hazard
nt_oversvamningsrisk_befolkning.note: Share of residents (2021 census) living in areas with a medium probability of flooding (scenario P2, return period 100–200 years) in ISPRA's national mosaic of the basin plans: 64,592 people; 83.9% live in low-probability areas (P1). Italy 11.5%, Veneto 11.7% (2021).

nt_pm10_overskridandedygn.name: Days with PM10 above the limit (worst station)
nt_pm10_overskridandedygn.note: Number of days with PM10 above 50 µg/m³ at the city's worst fixed monitoring station; the EU allows 35 a year. 70 days in 2022 and 62 in 2023. Italy: no national value for this measure; Veneto 8–66 days in its other six provincial capitals (2024).

nt_pm10_arsmedel.name: Annual mean PM10 (worst station)
nt_pm10_arsmedel.note: Highest annual mean of PM10 among the city's fixed monitoring stations (34 in 2022). The EU limit is 40 µg/m³ today and 20 µg/m³ from 2030; the WHO recommends 15. Italy: no national value for this measure; Veneto 21–35 µg/m³ in its other provincial capitals (2024).

nt_no2_arsmedel.name: Annual mean NO2 (worst station)
nt_no2_arsmedel.note: Highest annual mean of nitrogen dioxide among the city's fixed monitoring stations (37 in 2022). The EU limit is 40 µg/m³ today and 20 µg/m³ from 2030; the WHO recommends 10. Italy: no national value for this measure; Veneto 20–30 µg/m³ in its other provincial capitals (2024).

nt_anmalda_brott_per_100000.name: Reported offences per 100,000 inhabitants
nt_anmalda_brott_per_100000.note: Offences reported by the police to the judicial authorities per 100,000 registered residents (8,669.6 in 2023 and 5,534.4 in 2021); the rate is high because offences against the many visitors are counted against a small population. Italy 4,069.6, Veneto: not fetched (2024).

nt_fickstolder_per_100000.name: Reported pickpocketing per 100,000 inhabitants (province)
nt_fickstolder_per_100000.note: Reports of pickpocketing in the province per 100,000 inhabitants (ISTAT from the Ministry of the Interior's SDI register), more than three times the national level. Burglaries of homes: 347.9 (Italy 250.3, Veneto 327.6). Italy 236.8, Veneto 237.4 (2023).

nt_valdeltagande_kommunval.name: Turnout in the municipal election
nt_valdeltagande_kommunval.note: 112,767 of 201,713 eligible voters voted in the municipal election of 24–25 May 2026, in which the mayor was elected in the first round; turnout in 2020 was 62.23%. The electoral roll includes Italians living abroad, which lowers the share. Italy and Veneto: municipal elections are not held everywhere at once, so there is no comparable value (2026).

nt_valdeltagande_parlamentsval.name: Turnout in the general election (Chamber of Deputies)
nt_valdeltagande_parlamentsval.note: 124,105 of 187,202 eligible voters in the municipality voted for the Chamber of Deputies on 25 September 2022 (voters abroad are not included). Italy 63.91%, Veneto 70.17% (2022; Veneto's value is our own sum of the Veneto 1 and 2 constituencies).

nt_valdeltagande_europaval.name: Turnout in the European Parliament election
nt_valdeltagande_europaval.note: 92,711 of 197,090 eligible voters voted in the European Parliament election of 8–9 June 2024, the latest nationwide vote; the province 48.90%. Italy 49.69%, Veneto 52.60% (2024).

nt_kvinnor_kommunfullmaktige.name: Share of women in the municipal council (consiglio comunale)
nt_kvinnor_kommunfullmaktige.note: Own count in the Ministry of the Interior's register: 12 women among the 36 councillors elected in May 2026 (the mayor, a man, not counted); in the executive (giunta) 4 of the 10 assessori are women. Italy 35.4%, Veneto 37.9% of municipal councillors (August 2026, own count in the same register).

nt_bredband_ftth.name: Households with fibre-to-the-home coverage (FTTH, province)
nt_bredband_ftth.note: Share of households in the province living where a fibre-to-the-home (FTTH) connection is available, ISTAT's processing of the Agcom broadband map. Italy 70.7%, Veneto 64.9% (2024).

soc_pop_cs_1951.name: Population of Venice's historic centre (centro storico) in 1951
soc_pop_cs_1951.note: Registered residents on 31 December in the historic city: the six sestieri plus Giudecca and Sacca Fisola, without the Lido and the other islands. 1951 (census) is the Comune's index year (= 100) and the highest value in the series; 128,787 lived here in 1871 and 163,849 in 1936. The whole municipality had 315,811 inhabitants, the mainland 96,966.

soc_pop_cs_1966.name: Population of the centro storico in 1966
soc_pop_cs_1966.note: 31 December 1966. Since 1951 the population had fallen by 53,499 people, on average 3,567 a year (own calculation), while the mainland part of the municipality doubled from 96,966 to 193,314 inhabitants. The largest one-year drop in the series came in 1960–1961, with the 1961 census (−8,252).

soc_pop_cs_1971.name: Population of the centro storico in 1971
soc_pop_cs_1971.note: The Comune's registry figure for 31 December 1971. OCIO cites the 1971 census for the water city including Giudecca: about 35,000 dwellings, of which roughly 10,000 owner-occupied, 23,000 rented or lent and 1,000 empty. A 1973 CENSIS survey of those who left in 1964–68 found that 60.2% moved to get a healthier, more modern home.

soc_pop_cs_1981.name: Population of the centro storico in 1981
soc_pop_cs_1981.note: 31 December 1981. During the 1980s the population fell by an average of 1,695 people a year, to 76,644 in 1991 (own calculation). The figure 95,222, sometimes given for 1981, refers to 31 December 1980.

soc_pop_cs_1991.name: Population of the centro storico in 1991
soc_pop_cs_1991.note: 31 December 1991 (1990: 78,165). The district series give 455 births and 1,252 deaths that year, and 35,242 households of which 14,448 one-person (41.0%; sum of districts 1 and 2, own calculation).

soc_pop_cs_2001.name: Population of the centro storico in 2001
soc_pop_cs_2001.note: 31 December 2001. The figure 66,386, sometimes given for 2001, refers to 31 December 2000. 505 births and 1,037 deaths that year (sum of districts 1 and 2). In OCIO's reading of the 2001 census, owners lived in just under 18,000 dwellings, 10,000–11,000 were rented and more than 5,000 empty.

soc_pop_cs_2011.name: Population of the centro storico in 2011
soc_pop_cs_2011.note: 31 December 2011, less than half of the 121,309 of 1966 (−51%, own calculation). 421 births and 899 deaths that year (sum of districts 1 and 2). According to OCIO the 2011 census counted 8,909 rented dwellings in the water city, against about 23,000 in 1971.

soc_pop_cs_2022_below_50000.name: Population of the centro storico in 2022, the year it fell below 50,000
soc_pop_cs_2022_below_50000.note: 31 December 2022; a year earlier 50,434. The Comune publishes no date for the crossing; on 23 November 2022 OCIO wrote that the fall below the psychological 50,000 mark had produced a stream of articles and statements 'in recent weeks'. The association Venessia.com spreads the figure '49.999' on flags and posters as a symbol of the concern.

soc_pop_cs_2025.name: Population of the centro storico on 31 December 2025
soc_pop_cs_2025.note: In 2025 the population fell by 864 (−1.8%) from 48,489: 209 births, 689 deaths, 1,031 people moving in from other municipalities and abroad, 1,096 moving out, plus 600 moves in and 919 moves out within the municipality. That is 27.2% of the 1951 level and 19% of the municipality's residents (own calculations).

soc_pop_cs_2026_aug.name: Population of the centro storico on 31 August 2026 (latest monthly figure)
soc_pop_cs_2026_aug.note: −424 since the turn of the year; in August 2026 there were 14 births and 59 deaths in the centre. Whole municipality: 251,682. OCIO counts 46,964 residents in September 2026 (a different delimitation of the historic city), and the Venessia.com web counter showed 47,652 on 11 October 2026.

soc_pop_comune_peak_1968.name: The municipality's highest population (1968)
soc_pop_comune_peak_1968.note: The whole Comune di Venezia, then including Cavallino-Treporti, which became a separate municipality in 1999. The mainland (terraferma) had 200,445 inhabitants, the islands (estuario) 51,117 and the centre 116,270. 31 December 2025: 251,294, of which 178,131 on the mainland and 25,538 on the Lido, Pellestrina, Murano, Burano and the other islands.

soc_births_cs_2025.name: Births in the centro storico
soc_births_cs_2025.note: 4.3 per 1,000 inhabitants (own calculation with the mean population 48,057), against 5.6 in the province and 6.3 in Italy in 2024 (Eurostat, demo_r_gind3). The centre had 455 births in 1991, 505 in 2001, 421 in 2011 and 236 in 2021 (sum of districts 1 and 2). Whole municipality: 1,416.

soc_deaths_cs_2025.name: Deaths in the centro storico
soc_deaths_cs_2025.note: 14.3 per 1,000 inhabitants (own calculation), against 11.4 in the province and 11.1 in Italy in 2024 (Eurostat). 3.3 times as many people die as are born. 1,252 died in 1991, 899 in 2011 and 837 in 2021 (sum of districts 1 and 2). Whole municipality: 3,374.

soc_migration_external_cs_2025.name: Net migration with other municipalities and abroad, centro storico
soc_migration_external_cs_2025.note: 1,031 people moved in and 1,096 moved out. The municipality as a whole had positive net migration, 7,632 in and 6,181 out (+1,451), but the whole surplus went to the mainland (+1,671); the islands (estuario) had −155.

soc_moves_within_comune_cs_2025.name: Net moves to the rest of the municipality (mainland and islands), centro storico
soc_moves_within_comune_cs_2025.note: 600 moves into and 919 out of the two districts within the municipality (moves between the districts cancel out). The district tables give 309 arrivals from the rest of the municipality and 628 departures to it, 432 of them to the mainland (own sum). So every year a net of just over 300 Venetians move from the water city to Mestre, the Lido and the islands.

soc_natural_balance_comune_2025.name: Natural increase (births minus deaths) in the whole municipality
soc_natural_balance_comune_2025.note: 1,416 births and 3,374 deaths. Net migration of +1,451 offset most of it, so the population fell by 507 to 251,294 (31 December 2025). ISTAT's census-adjusted population was 249,490 on 1 January 2025. The number of foreign citizens rose by 1,591 during the year.

soc_natural_balance_cs_2015_2025.name: Natural decrease in the centro storico, total 2015–2025
soc_natural_balance_cs_2015_2025.note: 2,797 births and 8,810 deaths in 2015–2025. The flows sum to −8,669, which matches the change from the end of 2014 (56,311) to 2025, i.e. eleven years: on average 254 births and 801 deaths a year (own calculation). The natural decrease accounts for seven tenths of the decline; the rest is net moves to the rest of the municipality (−3,819), partly offset by net migration with other municipalities and abroad (+1,163). Municipality: −21,224.

soc_moves_within_comune_cs_2015_2025.name: Net moves to the rest of the municipality, centro storico, total 2015–2025
soc_moves_within_comune_cs_2015_2025.note: 7,978 moves into and 11,797 out of the centre within the municipality in 2015–2025, on average −347 a year over eleven years (own calculation). The mainland gained 3,103 and the islands 716 from moves within the municipality over the same period.

soc_migration_external_cs_2015_2025.name: Net migration with other municipalities and abroad, centro storico, total 2015–2025
soc_migration_external_cs_2015_2025.note: 11,830 arrivals and 10,667 departures in 2015–2025 (+106 a year over eleven years, own calculation). Over the period more people arrived in the centre from outside than left it for other municipalities; in 2025, however, the net was −65. Whole municipality: +8,656, of which +8,022 on the mainland.

soc_share_0_14_cs_2025.name: Share of children aged 0–14 in the centro storico
soc_share_0_14_cs_2025.note: 4,034 of 47,625 residents (sum of the classes 0–4, 5–9 and 10–14 in the Comune's table; own calculation). Whole municipality 10.3%; province 11.0%, Veneto 11.8% and Italy 11.9% (Eurostat, 1 January 2025). In the centre the share was 11.0% in 2011.

soc_share_65plus_cs_2025.name: Share of residents aged 65 and over in the centro storico
soc_share_65plus_cs_2025.note: 15,785 of 47,625 (own calculation). Whole municipality 28.7%; province 26.5%, Veneto 24.9% and Italy 24.7% (Eurostat, 1 January 2025). There are 391 people aged 65+ per 100 children aged 0–14 (municipality 280). The share in the centre was 26.8% in 2001 and 29.5% in 2011.

soc_share_80plus_cs_2025.name: Share of residents aged 80 and over in the centro storico
soc_share_80plus_cs_2025.note: 5,814 people (own calculation), of whom 1,136 are 90 or older (2.4%). Whole municipality 10.3%; province 8.7%, Veneto 8.0% and Italy 7.8% (Eurostat, 1 January 2025).

soc_households_cs_2025.name: Registered households (famiglie anagrafiche) in the centro storico
soc_households_cs_2025.note: Average household size 1.80 people (municipality 1.97). In 2000 there were 32,608 households; their number has fallen by 19%, the population by 28% (own calculation).

soc_one_person_households_cs_2025.name: Share of one-person households in the centro storico
soc_one_person_households_cs_2025.note: 14,801 of 26,499 households (own calculation). The number of one-person households has stayed around 14,400–15,200 since 1991, while the share rose from 41.0% (1991) and 44.6% (2001). Whole municipality 48.4% (61,842 households). How many people living alone are 65+ is not published by zone.

soc_foreign_residents_cs_2025.name: Foreign citizens registered in the centro storico
soc_foreign_residents_cs_2025.note: 9.7% of residents (own calculation), against 17.2% in the whole municipality (43,255), where most live on the mainland. In the centre the number has stayed around 4,600 since 2011 (4,564); in 2000 it was 2,062.

soc_born_in_venice_cs_2025.name: Share of centro storico residents born in Venice
soc_born_in_venice_cs_2025.note: 30,342 of 47,625 residents were born in Venice ('nativi'). In 2010 the share was 69.3% (41,332 of 59,621). Whole municipality 57.4%.

soc_projection_comune_2050.name: Population on 1 January 2050 according to ISTAT's municipal projection (base 2025)
soc_projection_comune_2050.note: Median scenario: 249,490 (1 Jan 2025), 245,422 (2030), 237,171 (2040) and 228,172 (2050), −8.5% in 25 years. It assumes 1,394–1,563 births and 3,375–3,521 deaths a year and net migration of +933 to +1,336 a year. ISTAT's earlier experimental projection (base 2022, published by the Comune) gave 235,713 in 2041. No projection exists for the centro storico.

soc_projection_share_65plus_comune_2040.name: Share aged 65+ in 2040 according to ISTAT's municipal projection
soc_projection_share_65plus_comune_2040.note: The share aged 65+ rises from 28.5% (2025) to 30.5% (2030) and 34.2% (2040) and stands at 33.7% in 2050; the mean age from 49.1 to 50.7. The share aged 80+ reaches 14.3% on 1 January 2050 (own calculation from ISTAT's five-year classes: 32,694 of 228,172), against 10.3% in 2025.

soc_projection_veneto_2080.name: Veneto's population in 2080 according to ISTAT's regional projection (base 2025)
soc_projection_veneto_2080.note: Median scenario: 4,853,472 (2025), 4,685,576 (2050), 4,084,694 (2080). The share aged 65+ rises from 24.9% to 34.4% (2050) and 35.8% (2080), 85+ from 4.1% to 8.1%. Life expectancy in 2080: men 87.4 and women 90.0; fertility 1.16 → 1.35 children per woman. Official projections end in 2080 and are not made for provinces.

soc_trend_pop_cs_2050.name: Population of the centro storico in 2050 if the 2015–2025 trend continues (trend line)
soc_trend_pop_cs_2050.note: No authority projects the centro storico. The decline in 2015–2025 was 1.53% a year (55,589 → 47,625); if it continues the population will be 44,082 in 2030, 37,766 in 2040 and 32,356 in 2050 (own calculation: 47,625 × 0.98466^(year − 2025)). A trend line, not a forecast; the 2011–2025 rate was almost the same (−1.52% a year).

soc_life_expectancy_men_province.name: Life expectancy at birth, men
soc_life_expectancy_men_province.note: ISTAT's life table for the province in 2025 (provisional estimate): 82.2 years (2024: 82.1), Veneto 82.5 and Italy 81.7. At age 65, 20.2 years remain (Italy 20.0). Figures for the municipality or the centre are not published.

soc_life_expectancy_women_province.name: Life expectancy at birth, women
soc_life_expectancy_women_province.note: ISTAT's life table for the province in 2025 (provisional estimate): 86.4 years (2024: 86.3), Veneto 86.5 and Italy 85.7. At age 65, 23.4 years remain (Italy 22.8). Both sexes: 84.2 years.

soc_avoidable_mortality_province.name: Avoidable mortality, ages 0–74
soc_avoidable_mortality_province.note: Age-standardised mortality from preventable or treatable causes (BES dei territori 2025): 15.5 in the province, 15.2 in Veneto and 17.6 in Italy per 10,000 inhabitants (2022); in 2021 the province's value was 17.8. Mortality from dementia and nervous-system diseases at 65+ is higher than nationally: 41.6 against 35.3.

soc_life_satisfaction_comune.name: Share of people 14+ highly satisfied with life (score 8–10)
soc_life_satisfaction_comune.note: ISTAT's small-area estimate for large municipalities (BesT): 52.6% of respondents give 8–10 on the 0–10 scale, against 55.2% in Italy; mean score 7.29 against 7.42 (own calculation from the counts per score). 6.7% did not answer. In 2022 the share was 54.7%.

soc_friends_to_count_on_comune.name: Share of people 14+ who have friends to count on
soc_friends_to_count_on_comune.note: ISTAT BesT (own calculation from the counts): 69.5% have friends to count on (Italy 74.4%) and 18.3% have none (Italy 15.0%). 83.7% have relatives to count on (Italy 87.0%) and 67.6% can count on one or more neighbours (Italy 70.9%). No direct measure of loneliness exists at municipal level.

soc_feel_safe_dark_comune.name: Share of people 14+ who feel safe walking alone in the dark where they live
soc_feel_safe_dark_comune.note: ISTAT BesT (own calculation): 11.5% very and 38.9% fairly safe, against 61.7% in Italy; 36.4% feel unsafe (Italy 27.6%) and 10.6% never go out alone or at all. 35.3% of households perceive a high or fairly high crime risk in their area (Italy 23.3%).

soc_hospital_beds_ss_giovanni_paolo.name: Hospital beds at the Ospedale Civile SS. Giovanni e Paolo
soc_hospital_beds_ss_giovanni_paolo.note: The island city's hospital in Castello, in the former Scuola Grande di San Marco, with an emergency department, maternity, paediatrics and geriatrics among 42 units; ULSS 3 states 'about 310 beds'. The province has 31.8 hospital beds per 10,000 inhabitants (Veneto 32.3, Italy 33.3; BES 2022) and 25.3 specialist doctors per 10,000 (Italy 34.1; 2023). I found no primary source for the number of water ambulances or their response times.

soc_dwellings_unoccupied_cs_2023.name: Share of dwellings without registered residents in the centro storico
soc_dwellings_unoccupied_cs_2023.note: ISTAT's permanent census of 31 December 2023, summed over the sections of the localities Venezia and Giudecca (own calculation): 42,431 dwellings, of which 26,552 occupied by at least one registered resident and 15,879 empty or used only by non-residents (second homes, tourist lets, students). Since 2021 ISTAT does not separate the two. The district Venezia-Murano-Burano: 36.2% (16,998 of 46,969); OCIO gives 21% for the island city in 2011.

soc_dwellings_unoccupied_comune_2023.name: Share of dwellings without registered residents in the whole municipality
soc_dwellings_unoccupied_comune_2023.note: 26,538 of 149,294 dwellings (own sum of ISTAT's 2023 section data). On the mainland 7.0–7.5% in each district, on the Lido–Pellestrina 24.9%. OCIO: 11% in 2011 and 17% in 2021 for the whole municipality; in 2021–2023 empty dwellings increased mainly on the mainland (+1,010).

soc_model_area_residents_2023.name: Registered residents within the model's 1.8 km square
soc_model_area_residents_2023.note: Sum for the 647 census sections (2021 boundaries) whose centroid lies within 45.426915–45.443085 N, 12.325979–12.349021 E, according to ISTAT's census of 31 December 2023 (own GIS calculation). 12,118 households, 6,738 people aged 65+ (31.7%) and 1,924 children aged 0–14; roughly 43% of the centre's residents.

soc_model_area_dwellings_unoccupied_2023.name: Share of dwellings without registered residents within the model's 1.8 km square
soc_model_area_dwellings_unoccupied_2023.note: 9,160 of 20,503 dwellings (ISTAT 2023, own GIS calculation as above) are empty or used only by non-residents, against 37.4% in the whole centre. 58.7% of households in the square are one-person. Inside Airbnb counts 3,786 listings in the same square (September 2026), 3,187 of them entire homes.

soc_tourist_beds_cs_2026.name: Tourist beds in the historic city
soc_tourist_beds_cs_2026.note: September 2026 according to OCIO's counter, based on the Comune's GeoIDS register: 25,447 beds in hotels, B&Bs and other establishments and 24,760 in tourist flats (locazioni turistiche). In April 2023 there were 44,484. The Comune does not publish the register as a table, hence a secondary source.

soc_tourist_beds_per_resident_cs_2026.name: Tourist beds per resident in the historic city
soc_tourist_beds_per_resident_cs_2026.note: 50,207 beds against 46,964 residents (OCIO, September 2026). The curves crossed in October 2024 at 48,469 beds against 48,451 residents – 'il sorpasso'. San Marco has 3.75 beds per resident, Dorsoduro 1.06, Santa Croce 1.05 and Giudecca 0.43. The historic city has 19% of the municipality's residents but 61% of its tourist beds. When the counter was new the press dated the crossing to September 2023 with different resident figures (see tur_baddar_fler_an_invanare_ar in turism-ekonomi.json).

soc_tourist_rental_units_cs_2026.name: Registered tourist flats (locazioni turistiche) in the historic city
soc_tourist_rental_units_cs_2026.note: September 2026 (OCIO/GeoIDS): 6,145 flats with 24,760 beds, against 5,040 and 19,016 in April 2023 (+30% beds). On 30 September 2025 OCIO counted 6,273. Share of tourist beds that are in flats: San Polo 70%, Castello 58%, Cannaregio 54%. Since 1 January 2025 every flat must have a national identification code (CIN). The Comune's tourism yearbook counts more, since it includes every dwelling open at any time in the year and the islands too (see tur_baddar_cs in turism-ekonomi.json).

soc_airbnb_entire_homes_cs_2026.name: Airbnb listings for entire homes in the centro storico
soc_airbnb_entire_homes_cs_2026.note: Inside Airbnb, 16 September 2026: 6,182 listings in the seven sestieri (with Giudecca), of which 5,151 entire homes (83%); 4,416 of them had a review in the last 12 months. Whole municipality 8,844 listings, 71% with hosts who have several listings; median nightly price for entire homes in the centre €283 (own calculations). That is 19 entire homes per 100 registered households in the centre.

soc_new_leases_comune_2025.name: New residential leases in the municipality
soc_new_leases_comune_2025.note: OMI 2025: 6,994 (−1.6%), of which 41% fixed-term leases at market terms (transitori, 2,878), 18% long market leases (1,255) and 41% leases with regulated rent (canone concordato: 1,222 short and 1,639 long). No breakdown by district is published.

soc_public_housing_comune_empty_2025.name: Municipally owned dwellings not let
soc_public_housing_comune_empty_2025.note: The Comune owns 5,348 dwellings (the list was published in 2025 after OCIO's freedom-of-information request); 1,143 (21%) were not let, 16% in the historic city. Half are in the island city. The average rent collected by the manager Insula was €195 a month, €228 in the centre. Since 2018 vacated 'non-ERP' dwellings have been let as social housing to middle-income households.

soc_public_housing_ater_empty_share_2025.name: Share of empty dwellings in ATER's stock in the municipality
soc_public_housing_ater_empty_share_2025.note: ATER Venezia (the regional public housing company) owns 5,163 dwellings in the municipality, half in the island city; 3,443 were let on 31 December 2025. The number of empty dwellings has grown by about 500 since 2022, while on average 34 a year were refurbished. Only 8 dwellings were allocated in 2025 (37 in 2024), after the Comune paused allocations following the Constitutional Court's April 2024 ruling on the residence requirement.

soc_public_housing_share_insular_2025.name: Share of households in the island city living in publicly owned housing
soc_public_housing_share_insular_2025.note: OCIO: 4,527 let dwellings owned by the Comune, ATER and IPAV (2025) against 29,971 dwellings occupied by registered residents (ISTAT 2023). The Comune's housing director spoke in September 2026 of '30% of residents'; OCIO disputes the comparison. Of the Comune's 2,571 dwellings in the island city 1,798 are let as social housing; of ATER's 2,590, 492 are (OCIO, 2025).

soc_erp_applicants_2025.name: Applicants in the queue for public housing (ERP)
soc_erp_applicants_2025.note: The Comune's provisional 2025 list according to OCIO: 517 applicants with an ISEE below €6,000 a year, 274 homeless or in temporary accommodation and 54 with an enforceable eviction order. About 1,200 applied for social housing. The queue has been around 2,000 since 2020; according to OCIO supply covers just over 10% of applicants.

soc_university_students_2025.name: Students enrolled at Ca' Foscari and IUAV
soc_university_students_2025.note: Academic year 2025/26: Ca' Foscari 18,900 and IUAV 4,951. In 2000/01: 25,172 (16,257 + 8,915). The figure refers to enrolment at the universities, not where students live; in the '9mq' survey (2023, 1,071 responses) 82% of respondents lived in the municipality, three in four of them on the islands. The Academy of Fine Arts and the Conservatory are not included.

soc_student_beds_esu.name: Student beds through ESU Venezia
soc_student_beds_esu.note: ESU Venezia (the regional student-support agency) offered 1,000 beds in 2023/24, 748 by selection and 252 reserved, including ESU places in residences run by others (the '9mq' report). About 4 beds per 100 students (own calculation with 23,851 enrolled in 2025/26). Private student residences: Camplus Santa Marta 650 beds, Ai Crociferi 255, San Giobbe 230, CX Mestre 568.

soc_turnout_european_2024_province.name: Turnout in the 2024 European Parliament election
soc_turnout_european_2024_province.note: BES dei territori 2025: 48.9% in the province, against 52.6% in Veneto and 49.8% in Italy; in 2019 it was 60.0%. Regional election 2020: 62.5%. Turnout in the municipal election of 24–25 May 2026 (55.9%, centre 53.97%, 2020: 62.2%) is in kommun-plats-historia.json.

soc_pupils_cs_primary_middle.name: Pupils in primary and lower-secondary schools in the centro storico
soc_pupils_cs_primary_middle.note: State and private schools with an address in the centre, school year 2024/25 (own sum of MIM open data per school): 2,570, against 3,611 in 2015/16 (−28.8%). The eleven state primary schools went from 1,789 to 1,209 pupils, the four state lower-secondary schools from 1,396 to 1,006. Upper-secondary schools in the centre have 6,319 pupils, many from the mainland.

soc_nonprofits_province.name: Non-profit organisations per 10,000 inhabitants
soc_nonprofits_province.note: BES dei territori 2025: 55.3 in the province, against 62.7 in Veneto and 61.0 in Italy (2022). The Comune's register of associations (Albo delle associazioni) has registration numbers up to 3,629 (September 2026), but the list also contains deregistered associations, so the number of active ones is unknown.

soc_graduate_migration_province.name: Net migration of young graduates (aged 25–39)
soc_graduate_migration_province.note: BES dei territori 2025: the province loses a net 11.3 Italian graduates aged 25–39 per 1,000 a year, against −5.2 in Veneto and −6.2 in Italy (2023); in 2021 the value was −7.9. The share of 25–39-year-olds with tertiary education is 32.1% (Italy 30.9%; 2024).

tur_presenze_comune_2025.name: Overnight stays in accommodation in the Municipality of Venice
tur_presenze_comune_2025.note: All registered overnight stays (presenze) in 2025 in hotels and other accommodation, short-term rentals included, in the whole municipality: the historic city with the islands, the Lido and the mainland. 5,858,665 arrivals and an average stay of 2.21 nights; −2.7% on the record year 2024 (13,290,973). Veneto had 74,157,123 overnight stays (Venice 17.4%) and Italy 476,853,549 (Venice 2.7%).

tur_presenze_comune_2019.name: Overnight stays in the Municipality of Venice 2019 (pre-pandemic)
tur_presenze_comune_2019.note: 5,523,283 arrivals and an average stay of 2.34 nights; the highest year before the pandemic, only surpassed in 2024. The municipality's series starts in 1949 with 1,389,831 overnight stays and passed 5 million in 1995 and 10 million in 2015.

tur_presenze_comune_2020.name: Overnight stays in the Municipality of Venice 2020 (pandemic year)
tur_presenze_comune_2020.note: −72.5% on 2019 and the lowest level since 1978. 1,337,626 arrivals: foreign arrivals fell by 80.7% and Italian ones by 44.3%, so the Italian share of arrivals rose from 13.5% to 31.1% (Annuario 2020).

tur_ankomster_cs_2025.name: Arrivals in accommodation in the historic city
tur_ankomster_cs_2025.note: Guests checking in to accommodation in the historic city including the smaller islands (Murano, Burano, Torcello etc.) in 2025, 67.9% of the municipality's arrivals; +1.8% on 2024 and +13.2% on 2019 (3,515,233, own calculation). 3,511,310 were foreign and 468,954 Italian.

tur_presenze_cs_2025.name: Overnight stays in the historic city
tur_presenze_cs_2025.note: Overnight stays in 2025 in the historic centre including the smaller islands, 72.5% of the municipality's total; −0.6% on 2024 (9,432,844) and +6.3% on 2019 (own calculation). Hotels had 4,555,016 and other accommodation 4,821,622; since 2024 other accommodation has had more overnight stays than hotels.

tur_presenze_cs_2019.name: Overnight stays in the historic city 2019 (pre-pandemic)
tur_presenze_cs_2019.note: 3,515,233 arrivals and an average stay of 2.51 nights. Hotels had 5.09 million overnight stays and other accommodation 3.73 million, of which short-term rental flats 2,128,255 (24%, own calculation).

tur_presenze_cs_2020.name: Overnight stays in the historic city 2020 (pandemic year)
tur_presenze_cs_2020.note: −71.3% on 2019; 923,304 arrivals and an average stay of 2.74 nights. About 72% of the guests were foreign, against almost 90% in a normal year.

tur_utlandska_andel_presenze_cs.name: Foreign guests' share of overnight stays in the historic city
tur_utlandska_andel_presenze_cs.note: 8,339,222 foreign overnight stays out of 9,376,638 in the historic centre in 2025 = 88.9%; for the whole municipality 86.6% (11,195,100 / 12,925,741). The largest markets in 2025 were the USA, Italy, France, the UK and Germany. In the pandemic year 2020 the share fell to about 72%.

tur_medelvistelse_cs.name: Average length of stay in the historic city
tur_medelvistelse_cs.note: Overnight stays per arrival in 2025; 2.51 in 2019 and 2.74 in the pandemic year 2020. Hotel guests stay 2.17 nights and guests in other accommodation 2.56; in the whole municipality 2.21 and on the mainland 1.82.

tur_korttidsuthyrning_andel_ankomster_cs.name: Short-term rental flats' share of arrivals in the historic city
tur_korttidsuthyrning_andel_ankomster_cs.note: Locazioni turistiche – flats let to tourists under regional law 11/2013 art. 27bis – received 1,252,286 of 3,980,264 arrivals and 3,371,970 overnight stays (36%, own calculation) in 2025. In 2019 the share of arrivals was 19.4% (682,097; Yearbook 2024 table 1.19). The category also includes lets longer than 30 days.

tur_baddar_cs.name: Tourist beds in the historic city
tur_baddar_cs.note: Beds in accommodation open at some point in 2025 in the historic centre with the islands: 20,896 in 331 hotels and 49,345 in other accommodation, of which 42,011 in 9,560 short-term rental flats. 59,373 beds in 2019 and 53,578 in the pandemic year 2021; +4,707 in 2025 alone. The whole municipality has 91,556.

tur_baddar_per_invanare_cs.name: Tourist beds per resident in the historic city
tur_baddar_per_invanare_cs.note: 70,241 beds divided by the 54,480 residents of the Venezia-Murano-Burano borough, which covers the same area as the historic centre of the tourism statistics (the municipality's population table by district 2015–2025) = 1.29. Against the 47,625 residents of the centro storico proper (the sestieri and Giudecca) it is 1.47. In 2015, 63,530 people lived in Venezia-Murano-Burano.

tur_baddar_fler_an_invanare_ar.name: Year tourist beds came to outnumber residents in the historic city (OCIO counters)
tur_baddar_fler_an_invanare_ar.note: The civic observatory OCIO's bed counter in a bookshop on Campo Santa Margherita showed 48,596 tourist beds against 49,365 residents (Venessia.com's counter) in April 2023, 49,693 against 49,304 in September and 50,016 against 49,211 in December 2023. OCIO counts hotels and short-term rentals from the municipal register; in 2008 there were about 12,000 beds and just over 60,000 residents (Il Post).

tur_gaster_per_natt_cs.name: Overnight guests per night in the historic city (annual average)
tur_gaster_per_natt_cs.note: 9,376,638 overnight stays / 365 = 25,689 guests per night on average in 2025, a little over half as many as the 47,625 residents of the centro storico; in the peak month of October about 31,500 per night (975,072 / 31). Day-trippers come on top of this (see tur_dagsbesokare_per_dag_2022).

tur_presenze_per_invanare.name: Overnight stays per resident in the Municipality of Venice
tur_presenze_per_invanare.note: 12,925,741 overnight stays divided by 251,294 residents on 31 December 2025 (the municipality's auditors) = 51.4; in the historic city with the islands 172 per resident (9,376,638 / 54,480). Venice is one of five Italian cities (with Rimini, Verbania, Florence and Pisa) where overnight stays are at least 20 times the population, the threshold for charging up to €10 per night in tourist tax under the 2023 budget law (Il Post).

tur_belaggning_hotell.name: Gross bed occupancy rate in hotels
tur_belaggning_hotell.note: Overnight stays / 365 / beds for the municipality's 33,320 hotel beds in 2025; 68.0% in the busiest month. 60.1% in 2024 and 66.0% in 2019. For all 91,556 beds 38.7% and for other accommodation including short-term rentals 28.5%.

tur_toppmanad_presenze_cs.name: Overnight stays in the historic city in the busiest month (October 2025)
tur_toppmanad_presenze_cs.note: October had the most overnight stays in 2025, ahead of July (942,427) and May (929,846); January the fewest (436,267), so the peak month has 2.2 times as many (own calculation). July had the most arrivals (427,099). Every month from April to October was above 898,000; in 2024 May was the largest (988,317).

tur_kryssning_2019.name: Cruise passengers at the Port of Venice 2019 (before the ban)
tur_kryssning_2019.note: Embarking, disembarking and transit cruise passengers on 500 calls in 2019, when large ships still passed through the Bacino di San Marco and the Giudecca Canal to the Marittima terminal. All port passengers: 1,822,703.

tur_kryssning_2025.name: Cruise passengers at the Port of Venice 2025
tur_kryssning_2025.note: 266 calls in 2025, +6.3% on 2024 but 64% fewer passengers than in 2019 (own calculation) since large cruise ships were shut out of the Bacino di San Marco and the Giudecca Canal in 2021; 5,237 in the pandemic year 2020. The port authority's accounts report 617,454 cruise movements in 2025 (542,496 home port, 74,958 transit) with a different definition. All port passengers: 708,267.

tur_biennale_konst_2024.name: Visitors to the Art Biennale (60th International Art Exhibition)
tur_biennale_konst_2024.note: 19 April–24 November 2024, −15.1% on the 2022 record (827,411); 593,616 in 2019. The 2025 Architecture Biennale had 280,770 visitors and the film festival on the Lido 254,443 spectators. The Biennale's venues lie at the eastern edge of the model area: the western part of the Arsenale on the edge and the Giardini just outside.

tur_dogepalatset_besokare.name: Visitors to the Doge's Palace (Palazzo Ducale)
tur_dogepalatset_besokare.note: +1.7% on 2024 and level with 2019 (1,351,656); 318,104 in 2020. All the Fondazione Musei Civici museums together had 2,393,315 visitors in 2025. The palace stands on the Piazzetta San Marco in the middle of the model area.

tur_san_marco_basilika_besokare.name: Visitors to the St Mark's Basilica complex
tur_san_marco_basilika_besokare.note: A joint ticket since 2025 for the basilica, the museum and the Pala d'Oro, of which the museum 444,627 and the Pala d'Oro 322,504. In 2024, 1,861,286 visits to the basilica itself were counted. The Campanile had 567,419 visitors in 2025.

tur_accademia_besokare.name: Visitors to the Gallerie dell'Accademia
tur_accademia_besokare.note: +16.3% on 2023 and 305,099 in 2019. The state's figures for 2025 were not available when the yearbook was published. The gallery stands by the Accademia bridge over the Grand Canal.

tur_guggenheim_besokare.name: Visitors to the Peggy Guggenheim Collection
tur_guggenheim_besokare.note: Palazzo Venier dei Leoni between the Accademia and the Salute; −11.8% on 2024 (388,630) and 350,475 in 2019.

tur_dagsbesokare_per_ar.name: Day-trippers (escursionisti) per year, estimate
tur_dagsbesokare_per_ar.note: Assessment in the study, after van der Borg (2017): almost 22 million day-trippers a year, against about 5 million in 1988. Day-trippers are not registered; the municipality's own estimate was about 53,000 per day (Tourist Report 2019). The figure is an assessment, not a count.

tur_dagsbesokare_per_dag_2022.name: Day-trippers per day in the historic city (annual average, mobile data)
tur_dagsbesokare_per_dag_2022.note: Measured with mobile-phone data: on average 61,461 day-trippers and 32,339 overnight tourists per day in the historic city in 2022; the newspaper gives a total of about 98,000 visitors per day. Bertocchi et al. (2020) gave 66,800 visitors and tourists plus 20,500 commuting workers and students per day (2018).

tur_besokare_toppdag_2022.name: Visitors in the historic city on the busiest day of the year (30 October 2022)
tur_besokare_toppdag_2022.note: All Saints' weekend 2022: 54,253 overnight tourists and 88,993 day-trippers according to the same mobile-data study. With about 49,000–50,000 residents (the municipality: 55,589 in 2015 and 47,625 in 2025) that is roughly three visitors per resident that day (own rough calculation).

tur_barkraft_per_dag.name: Tourism carrying capacity of the historic city (visitors per day)
tur_barkraft_per_dag.note: Optimum in a fuzzy linear-programming model: 15,500 hotel guests, 22,000 guests in other accommodation and 14,611 day-trippers per day, in all 19.0 million visitors a year of whom 28% day-trippers. The bottlenecks are St Mark's Square, vaporetto capacity, restaurants, parking and waste handling. The first calculation in 1988 gave about 10 million visitors a year.

tur_cda_betalningar_2024.name: Paid access fees for day-trippers 2024 (first trial year)
tur_cda_betalningar_2024.note: 29 fee days from 25 April 2024 at €5, on average 16,676 payers per day; €2,249,505 according to the municipality's summary (the accounts report €2.43 million). According to Il Post, setting up and running the scheme cost at least €3 million in the first year.

tur_cda_betalningar_2025.name: Paid access fees for day-trippers 2025
tur_cda_betalningar_2025.note: Provisional for 54 days from 18 April to 27 July 2025: 704,467 through the platform (51% at €5, 49% at €10) and 19,030 through agreements; on average 13,046 per day, most on Friday 2 May (24,951). Overnight guests registered as exempt at an average of 36,639 per day. The accounts report €5.44 million.

tur_cda_betalningar_2026.name: Paid access fees for day-trippers 2026
tur_cda_betalningar_2026.note: 60 fee days from 3 April to 26 July 2026 (every Friday–Sunday plus 27–30 April and 1–4 June, 8.30–16.00): 316,099 (46.5%) at €5 with advance booking and 363,454 at €10, in all €5,215,035, according to the municipality's provisional summary. Fewer payments than in 2025 despite six more days. The fee only applies to the Città antica, not Murano, Burano or the Lido; overnight guests, Veneto residents, students, commuters and children under 14 do not pay.

tur_cda_intakter_2025.name: The municipality's revenue from the access fee (contributo di accesso)
tur_cda_intakter_2025.note: Accrued revenue (accertamenti) in the 2025 accounts, against €2.43 million in 2024; 1.6% of tax revenue excluding the casino. After running costs part goes to a lower waste charge (TARI): €1.0 million in the 2025 TARI budget (the municipality's summary speaks of at least €1.5 million) and €1,771,000 of the 2026 revenue, which was €5,215,035.

tur_cda_snitt_per_dag_2026.name: Paying day-trippers per fee day 2026
tur_cda_snitt_per_dag_2026.note: −17% on 2025 (13,398) and −32% on 2024 according to the municipality, which notes that the years are not directly comparable: Fridays were not included in 2024 and 2026 had more weekdays. Saturdays 13,661 on average; May 13,940, June 10,179 and July 9,597 per day. The municipality's 2025 summary gave 13,046 for platform purchases.

tur_cda_dagar_over_20000.name: Fee days with at least 20,000 paying day-trippers
tur_cda_dagar_over_20000.note: 4 of 29 days (13.8%) in 2024, 3 of 54 (5.6%) in 2025 and 1 of 60 (1.7%) in 2026: Saturday 2 May 2026 with 25,471. The second-largest day in 2026 had 18,969 and the smallest (Wednesday 29 April) 7,441. The municipality sees signs that the peaks are being damped; the evaluation is being done with CISET (Ca' Foscari, Regione Veneto and Touring Club Italiano).

tur_imposta_soggiorno_2025.name: The municipality's revenue from the tourist tax (imposta di soggiorno)
tur_imposta_soggiorno_2025.note: Accrued revenue 2025: €38.38 million plus €0.32 million in recovered arrears, −€1.6 million on 2024 (39.70 + 0.58) and €38.19 million in 2023. The tourist tax provides 11.4% of the municipality's tax revenue excluding the casino (€353.2 million). €5.5 million of earmarked tourist tax was used in 2025 to lower the waste charge (TARI).

tur_kommunens_lopande_intakter.name: The municipality's current revenue (entrate correnti)
tur_kommunens_lopande_intakter.note: Accrued revenue 2025: taxes €471.0 million, transfers €207.3 million and other revenue €193.6 million; €825.1 million in 2024 and €818.9 million in 2023. The accounts (approved by the council on 23 April 2026) closed with a result (risultato di amministrazione) of €529.3 million, of which €25.5 million unrestricted. Staff costs were €114.7 million.

tur_turistskatter_andel_intakter.name: Tourist tax and access fee as a share of the municipality's current revenue
tur_turistskatter_andel_intakter.note: (€38.71 million in tourist tax + €5.44 million in access fees) / €871.83 million in current revenue = 5.1% in 2025 (own calculation from the accounts). The casino's gross takings correspond to 13.5%, but most of that goes back to the operating company (see tur_kasino_spelintakter).

tur_kasino_spelintakter.name: Gaming revenue from the Casinò di Venezia
tur_kasino_spelintakter.note: Of the 2025 gaming revenue, €88.3 million (75%) went as a fee to the operating company and €9.4 million in taxes, leaving €20.1 million net for the municipality, against €15.6 million in 2019 and −€0.7 million in 2020. The casino's historic seat, Ca' Vendramin Calergi, stands on the Grand Canal at the northern edge of the model area.

tur_sysselsatta_foretag.name: Persons employed in business local units in the Municipality of Venice
tur_sysselsatta_foretag.note: Employees and self-employed (addetti) in 25,729 local units in 2022 according to ISTAT's territorial Frame SBS, with €6.76 billion in value added and €59,400 per person employed. Public administration, agriculture and finance are not included, so the staff of the municipality, the health service and the universities are missing here. ISTAT classes the Venezia local labour system as 'urbano prevalentemente portuale' (urban, mainly port).

tur_sysselsatta_hotell_restaurang_andel.name: Accommodation and food services: share of persons employed in business
tur_sysselsatta_hotell_restaurang_andel.note: 20,617 of the 113,676 persons employed in business local units worked in accommodation and food services (ATECO I) in 2022 = 18.1%, against 8.9% in Italy and 8.7% in Veneto (summed from ISTAT's provincial tables). Pay per employee in the sector was €21,500 against an average of €29,000 for the municipality's businesses.

tur_sysselsatta_handel_andel.name: Wholesale and retail trade: share of persons employed in business
tur_sysselsatta_handel_andel.note: 18,518 of 113,676 persons employed in trade (ATECO G) in 2022 = 16.3% (Italy 19.5%, Veneto 17.8%).
