Transport and storage – the port, the airport and public transport – has 14,296 = 12.6% (Italy 6.6%, Veneto 5.7%), business support services 13,340 and professional and technical services (ATECO M) 10,131.

tur_sysselsatta_tillverkning_andel.name: Manufacturing: share of persons employed in business
tur_sysselsatta_tillverkning_andel.note: 9,876 of 113,676 persons employed in manufacturing and mining (ATECO B–C) in 2022 = 8.7%, against 21.6% in Italy and 30.9% in Veneto; all industry including construction, energy and waste 20,369 (17.9%). Value added per person employed in manufacturing was €90,400, more than twice that in accommodation and food services (€42,600).

tur_hotell_restaurang_andel_foradlingsva.name: Accommodation and food services: share of business value added
tur_hotell_restaurang_andel_foradlingsva.note: €877.7 million of the €6,757.0 million in value added in the municipality's businesses in 2022 = 13.0% (Italy 4.0%, Veneto 4.1%). It only measures the direct visitor economy; trade, transport, museums and crafts selling to visitors are not included, so tourism's real share is larger. No official tourism satellite account for the municipality was found.

tur_inkomst_per_skattebetalare.name: Average taxable income per taxpayer
tur_inkomst_per_skattebetalare.note: Taxable income (reddito imponibile) of €5,156,700,571 divided by the 190,227 filers with taxable income, income year 2024. Veneto €25,885 and Italy €24,893; Padua €31,270 and Treviso €31,717. Venice had €23,482 in 2019. Employees earned €24,505 on average, less than in Veneto (€25,249).

tur_arbetsloshet_provins.name: Unemployment rate, age 15–74, Metropolitan City of Venice
tur_arbetsloshet_provins.note: ISTAT labour force survey: 4.6% in 2025, 3.9% in 2024 and 6.0% in 2019. Veneto 3.4% and Italy 6.1% in 2025.

tur_ungdomsarbetsloshet_provins.name: Youth unemployment rate, age 15–24, Metropolitan City of Venice
tur_ungdomsarbetsloshet_provins.note: 24.7% in 2025 and 27.1% in 2024, against 13.7% in Veneto and 20.6% in Italy in 2025. Provincial figures for young people rest on small samples and swing between years.

tur_hamn_gods.name: Cargo throughput at the Port of Venice
tur_hamn_gods.note: +4.9% on 2024: commercial cargo +8.5% while industrial (−5.3%) and oil (−1.2%) traffic fell. Container traffic was 532,778 TEU (478,839 in 2024). With Chioggia the port authority handled 26.2 million tonnes.

tur_marghera_sysselsatta_1965.name: Persons employed in the Porto Marghera industrial area at the 1965 peak
tur_marghera_sysselsatta_1965.note: The municipality's historical series: 3,440 employed in 1925, 22,500 in 1950, the peak of 32,980 in 229 firms in 1965, 29,000 in 1980, 18,814 in 1990 and 12,958 in 1998. Parts of the area are still called Raffinerie, Vecchio and Nuovo Petrolchimico.

tur_marghera_sysselsatta_2018.name: Persons employed in the Porto Marghera industrial area 2018
tur_marghera_sysselsatta_2018.note: Persons employed in 915 firms on 31 December 2018, including workers on short-time support: a third of the 1965 peak; the low point was 10,060 in 2014. There are four times as many firms, but smaller. No later edition of the municipality's survey was found.

tur_studenter_cafoscari.name: Students at Ca' Foscari University
tur_studenter_cafoscari.note: Enrolled in bachelor's, master's and single-cycle programmes in the 2025/26 academic year (11,629 women and 7,271 men); 21,121 in 2019/20. Doctoral students and single courses are not included. The main building, Ca' Foscari, stands on the Grand Canal in the western part of the model area.

tur_studenter_iuav.name: Students at the Università Iuav di Venezia
tur_studenter_iuav.note: Iuav (architecture, design, planning, arts and theatre) in the 2025/26 academic year: 3,039 women and 1,912 men, against 3,935 in 2019/20; 172 teaching staff and 241 technical-administrative staff in 2024 (ANVUR). Together with Ca' Foscari 23,851 students, about half as many as the residents of the centro storico, though many live on the mainland (own comparison).

tur_murano_ugnar.name: Glass furnaces (fornaci) on Murano
tur_murano_ugnar.note: In February 2024 the Promovetro consortium counted 151 glass firms on Murano: 64 furnaces and 87 secondary processing firms (lampwork, fusing, mirrors, grinding, decoration) employing 1,242 people. According to the same source, 80% of the glass objects in Venice's shops are not made on Murano. In the early 2000s there were about a hundred furnaces (Insula).

tur_murano_sysselsatta.name: Persons employed in Murano's glass firms
tur_murano_sysselsatta.note: Banca Ifis counts 160 active glass firms employing 928 people in 2025, against 114 firms and 819 employed in 2015; turnover rose from about €104 million to €180 million, and to €288 million including the supply chain. Promovetro gives 1,242 employed (2024) with a wider definition. Energy and utilities are 13% of the value in the supply chain.

tur_murano_sysselsatta_1971.name: Persons employed in Murano's glass industry 1971
tur_murano_sysselsatta_1971.note: About 4,000 employed in Murano's glass industry in the 1950s, 3,142 in 1971, 2,290 in 1981 and about 2,000 in the 1990s; in the early 2000s Promovetro had just under 200 member firms employing about 1,600. In the 1960s 24% of the firms had more than 100 employees; today small firms dominate.

tur_gondoljarer_auktoriserade.name: Authorised gondoliers
tur_gondoljarer_auktoriserade.note: Gondoliers holding a licence according to EFE in October 2026, when the municipality opened a new 40-hour 'Arte del gondoliere' course; the municipality's 2020 regulation allows 440 licences (see en_gondol_licenser in energi-resor.json). Since Giorgia Boscolo became the first woman gondolier in 2009, 14 more women have followed. A 30-minute ride cost €90 in the daytime and €110 after 7 pm (dpa, 2024).

tur_souvenirbutiker_andel.name: Souvenir shops' share of retail in the historic city
tur_souvenirbutiker_andel.note: 299 of the 2,876 retail businesses in the Chamber of Commerce register (January 2021) sold souvenirs, trinkets and costume jewellery, against 141 craft shops (4.9%); food, drink and tobacco were 13.9%. Hotels, restaurants and retail made up 58% of the historic city's 10,232 registered businesses.

tur_vardagsbutiker_2007.name: Grocery and other everyday shops in the historic city 2007
tur_vardagsbutiker_2007.note: 720 shops in 1976 and 276 in 2007 (−62%), while shops for tourists rose from 303 to 997 (+229%), 'banal' souvenir shops by 265%. Already in 1971–1981 the share of services aimed at residents fell from 46.9% to 37.7% (Andreozzi et al. 1983).

tur_osm_presentbutiker_per_matbutik.name: Gift shops per food shop in the model area (OpenStreetMap)
tur_osm_presentbutiker_per_matbutik.note: Inside the model's bounding box: 119 gift shops and 15 variety stores against 84 food shops (19 supermarkets, 18 convenience stores, 18 bakeries, 10 delis, 8 greengrocers, 8 pastry shops, 2 fishmongers, 1 butcher) = 1.6. 785 shops in all, of which 151 clothes shops and 53 jewellers, plus 205 hotels and 374 restaurants. OSM is mapped by volunteers and incomplete.

avfolkning.title: A city emptying of its people
avfolkning.text: The historic city has 47,625 residents, a quarter of the 174,808 who lived here in 1951, and loses 500–900 a year. In 2025, 209 children were born and 689 people died; seven tenths of the decline since 2015 is deaths outnumbering births, so the city needs young people and families to move in. If the trend continues, about 32,000 will live here in 2050.

bostader.title: Homes that become tourist beds
bostader.text: 37.4% of the historic city's 42,431 homes have no registered resident, and since 2023–2024 there have been more tourist beds than residents. Short-term lets took 31.5% of tourist arrivals in 2025, against 19.4% in 2019, and a home in the centre costs 4,332 euros per square metre, against 1,660 on the mainland. Meanwhile about 2,900 municipal and regional public homes in the municipality stand empty awaiting renovation, while 2,251 households are on the waiting list.

besokare.title: More visitors than the city can carry
besokare.text: On an ordinary day in 2022 an average of 61,461 day visitors came to the historic city, and on the busiest day 143,246 visitors were there – about three per resident. The city had 9.38 million guest nights in 2025, nine in ten of them by foreign guests, and a 2020 study put its carrying capacity at about 52,000 visitors a day. The access fee for day visitors applied on 60 days in 2026 and is still a trial.

havet.title: The sea is rising and MOSE closes ever more often
havet.text: MOSE closed 49 times in the 2025/26 season, but the barriers were built for 3–5 closures a year and for a sea rising 60 cm in a hundred years. With the sea 50 cm higher they would have to close on average once a day, and at tides between 80 and 110 cm, when they stay open, St Mark's Square floods. The sea now stands 35 cm higher against the city's stones than in 1897 and has risen 4.8 mm a year since 1993.

lagunen.title: A lagoon turning into a shallow sea
lagunen.text: The salt marshes have shrunk from 158 km² in 1912 to about 40 km², and the lagoon loses a net 0.8 million m³ of sediment a year – the rivers bring only 30,000 m³. None of the lagoon's eleven classified water bodies has good ecological status, and while MOSE is closed the salt marshes miss the silt that storm surges would otherwise carry to them: their growth falls by at least 25%.

aldrande.title: An ageing city – with bridges of steps
aldrande.text: 33.1% of the historic city's residents are 65 or older and 12.2% are 80 or older, against 24.7% and 7.8% in Italy, and only 8.5% are under 15. More than half of the households are one person, and the schools in the centre have 28.8% fewer pupils than in 2015/16. 95% of the 244 bridges in the central city have steps, and by water bus a wheelchair user can reach about 70% of the city – without a boat, 2%.

batar.title: Wakes and exhaust on the canals
batar.text: Boats and ships produce 46.7% of the municipality's nitrogen oxides and 39.1% of its particles, and by the Rio Novo canal nitrogen dioxide was 34 µg/m³ in 2025 – 70% above the EU limit from 2030. ACTV has 148 passenger boats but only one hybrid vaporetto in service, and the city council is asking for money against the wakes that wear down the quay walls.

varldsarvet.title: The World Heritage
varldsarvet.text: Venice and its Lagoon became a World Heritage Site in 1987, and 2,742 buildings in the city and the lagoon are listed; 83% of the historic city's residential buildings were built before 1919. The motto 'com'era, dov'era' – as it was, where it was – has guided rebuilding from the Campanile in 1912 to La Fenice in 2003.

till_fots.title: A city on foot and on the water
till_fots.text: The historic city has no cars: of some 100,000 people who arrive at Piazzale Roma, Tronchetto and the station on an ordinary weekday, 64.5% walk on and the rest take a boat. The municipality has 707 public-transport trips per resident a year, the most in Italy, and 460 cars per 1,000 residents, the fewest of Italy's provincial capitals (country 701).

lagunarbetet.title: MOSE and half a century of lagoon work
lagunarbetet.text: Since 3 October 2020 MOSE has protected the city from most tides above 110 cm, and its first hundred raisings are estimated to have prevented 2.6 billion euros of damage. On 22 November 2022 the sea stood at 173 cm outside the lagoon but only 66 cm in the city. Since the Special Law of 1973 the state has also raised 100 km of quays and shores and rebuilt 16 km² of salt marsh.

lagunens_natur.title: The lagoon's nature and food
lagunens_natur.text: 62% of the municipality's area is protected nature, almost the whole lagoon is a bird protection area, and some 24,000 flamingos wintered there in 2025. The Rialto market has been there since 1097, Sant'Erasmo has been Venice's kitchen garden since the 1500s with its purple artichoke, and 28 fish farms (valli da pesca) work 9,284 hectares of the lagoon.

universiteten.title: The universities and research
universiteten.text: 23,851 students are enrolled at Ca' Foscari and IUAV, as many as half the historic city's population. The VSF foundation wants to make Venice a university city – Venezia città campus – and the mayor wants to turn the old hospital on the Lido into a research centre with hundreds of specialists.

offentliga_bostader.title: Homes to give back
offentliga_bostader.text: The municipality owns 5,348 homes and the regional housing company ATER 5,163 in the municipality, half of them in the island city, and about 2,900 stand empty awaiting renovation. In 2022 Venice became the first city in Italy with the right to limit short-term lets (Article 37-bis of Decree-Law 50/2022), and the new administration wants to renovate empty municipal flats for young couples.

besoksverktyg.title: Tools for the visitors
besoksverktyg.text: The access fee for day visitors has been tried since 2024, and the days with more than 20,000 paying have fallen from four to one; in 2025 it brought in 5.4 million euros and the tourist tax 38.7 million. Since August 2021 ships over 25,000 gross tonnes may not pass through the San Marco basin and the Giudecca canal, and cruise passengers fell from 1.6 million in 2019 to 0.57 million in 2025.

kommun_vision.title: Casa, mobilità e lavoro – housing, mobility and work (2026–2031)
kommun_vision.text: The new administration sums up its vision in three pillars – housing, mobility and work – to strengthen the middle class both in the city on the water and on the mainland. Empty municipal flats are to be renovated and given above all to young couples, qualified jobs are to be drawn to the city, among them to a research centre in the old hospital on the Lido, and abandoned sites such as the old gasholders and Sant'Elena are to be brought back to life. The mayor wants stable funding for the Special Law for Venice and to leave a stronger, less indebted municipality to the next generation. The programme for the term, with eleven areas from housing and tourism to the environment, goes before the city council on 15 October 2026.

kommun_vision.title: The PAESC climate plan – emissions 72% lower by 2030, climate neutral by 2050
kommun_vision.text: The climate plan the municipal giunta adopted in January 2026 has 33 measures to cut the municipality's carbon dioxide emissions by 72% by 2030 compared with 2005, and the municipality has committed to being climate neutral by 2050. 46 measures are to adapt the city to twelve climate risks, from heatwaves and cloudbursts to tides and the rising sea. Among the goals are more trees, a hydrogen valley in Porto Marghera and hybrid engines on every boat on the Grand Canal by 2032.

kommun_vision.title: Venezia Capitale Mondiale della Sostenibilità
kommun_vision.text: The foundation was set up on 14 March 2022 to make Venice a model of sustainable development – environmental, economic and social. It brings together the region, the municipality, the universities, the Fondazione Giorgio Cini and large companies in nine areas, among them hydrogen in Porto Marghera, protecting the lagoon's ecosystem, a university city (Venezia città campus), countering depopulation and protecting homes from short-term lets, and managing the flows of visitors. The foundation calls the city a living laboratory on a small scale with global visibility.

kommun_vision.title: The Special Law for Venice – the council's own list of needs
kommun_vision.text: Since 2020 the city council has four times asked the state to fund the Special Law for Venice steadily and over several years, most recently on 23 July 2026. The list is the city's own picture of what is needed: quays, bridges and walkways; dredging the canals and fighting the wakes; the fire-water network; support for the people who live here and measures against depopulation; trade and crafts that suit the city; the islands; the lagoon's ecosystem and adaptation to the rising sea.
